The group said its protest on Tuesday followed the DMO’s failure to provide a substantive response to a Freedom of Information (FOI) request submitted on 19 August 2026.
The request sought access to records on public debt management, financial reporting, debt issuances and the reconciliation of debt figures.
Addressing journalists during the demonstration, GIW country representative, Comrade Eneji Mohammed, who read a statement on behalf of the organisation’s executive director, Comrade Abraham Temitayo Adewoye, said the request was informed by issues raised in the Auditor-General for the Federation’s 2024 Annual Report on Non-Compliance.
Mohammed said the organisation wanted documentary explanations and supporting records to establish what had happened, what had been reconciled and which issues remained outstanding. He stressed that GIW was not accusing any individual or institution of wrongdoing but was demanding information necessary for public accountability.
Among its demands, the group asked the DMO to provide its annual reports and audited financial statements for 2020 to 2025, including relevant audit opinions and supporting schedules.
Mohammed said: “Our request was informed by issues raised in the Auditor-General for the Federation’s 2024 Annual Report on Non-Compliance. These matters require documentary explanations and proper reconciliation from the relevant authorities.
“We have requested records relating to the reported ₦88.674 trillion in new debt issues and the ₦4.265 trillion debt-stock discrepancy identified in the audit material. We are not here to pronounce anyone guilty.
“We are here to demand the records, explanations and supporting documents needed to establish what happened, what has been reconciled and what remains outstanding.”
He disclosed that GIW intended to subject the annual reports and financial statements obtained from the DMO to an independent forensic examination to assess the audit observations and determine whether outstanding issues had been adequately addressed.
He said the findings would subsequently be made available to Nigerian taxpayers and the general public, with clear distinctions between documented facts, audit observations, management explanations and unresolved matters.
Mohammed maintained that the campaign was not intended to undermine the Federal Government but to strengthen public institutions and promote responsible governance.
According to GIW, accountability should not rest solely on the President, as every public institution has a responsibility to maintain proper records, manage public funds responsibly and respond to legitimate requests for information.
The organisation also announced plans to extend its accountability campaign to other public agencies from Wednesday, 18 November, following resolutions reached at its emergency meeting in the United Kingdom on 15 November.
It said it would also consider submitting documented complaints regarding unresolved accountability issues to relevant international institutions and the United Kingdom Government, including 10 Downing Street in London.
Mohammed insisted that the organisation would not abandon its campaign despite possible intimidation, stressing that Nigerians had the right to know how public agencies managed public resources.
Responding to the protesters, the Director of the DMO’s Portfolio Management Department, Elizabeth Ipeyong, said the office was transparent and accountable, adding that its borrowings were undertaken in accordance with provisions of the national budget.
She said most of the information requested by GIW, including the office’s annual reports and debt figures, was available on its official website.
Ipeyong, however, assured the protesters that the DMO would review the FOI request and provide additional explanations on the issues raised.
She said: “We have the information you are requesting. We manage funds on behalf of the government, and debt is a tool for economic growth. We borrow to grow Nigeria, and every borrowing is undertaken in accordance with the laws governing public borrowing in the country.”
She commended the protesters for conducting themselves peacefully, describing GIW and the DMO as partners working towards the country’s development.
Similarly, the Deputy Director of the Portfolio Management Department, Isiaku Muhammad, appealed to GIW to give the office more time to address the issues raised.
Muhammad said the DMO was already working on the request alongside earlier submissions and compiling the necessary information for a response.
He assured the protesters that the office would address their concerns, adding that both parties shared the objective of promoting good governance and accountability.
Also speaking, the Head of the DMO’s Internal Audit and Control Unit, Adeoye Felix, reiterated that the annual reports and other relevant information were available on the office’s website.
He urged GIW to identify any specific information missing from the website so that the DMO could address the gaps.
Despite the assurances, GIW announced that it would return to the DMO on Wednesday, 18 November, to continue its demand for the requested information.
The organisation urged the DMO leadership to provide the records or formal explanations where any information could not lawfully be disclosed.
